events.event_narrative: Strong winds occurred across Utah's northwest desert for several hours, with peak recorded wind gusts across the area of 80 mph at the SR-30 at Curlew sensor, 73 mph at Promontory Point, 64 mph along Interstate 80 at Milepost 29 sensor, 63 mph at Hat Island, and many gusts in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet in the 60-69 mph range.

Peak wind gusts across the area included 68 mph at the Snowbasin-Straw Top sensor and 67 mph at the Red Spur RAWS. In addition, all nine lifts at Snowbasin Resort were shut down due to the strong winds.

Peak wind gusts across the area included 97 mph on Mount Baldy, and many other gusts in the 50 to 65 mph range. Ski lifts were shut down at multiple mountain resorts, and the strong winds knocked down several large trees in Little Cottonwood Canyon.
The US-40 at Starvation sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 64 mph.

Strong winds in Emery County caused damage in several locations from Huntington to Ferron. Damages included many fences that were blown down, multiple traffic signs bent or broken, and significant damage to at least one roof. In addition, at least one parked trailer was flipped over, and multiple power transmission lines were damaged, resulting in a power outage for around 2,500 people. The top recorded wind gust in this part of the state was 54 mph at Carbon County Regional Airport/Buck Davis Field.
Peak wind gusts across the area included 59 mph at the Delta Bus Garage and 58 mph at Fish Springs in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
The Olympus Hills sensor recorded a wind gust of 63 mph.
The Vernon RAWS recorded a peak wind gust of 60 mph.
The Eyring Science Center sensor in Provo recorded a 60 mph wind gust. In addition, multiple large trees were knocked down in the Orem area from this early morning thunderstorm.
A sensor in Saratoga Springs recorded a peak wind gust of 63 mph.
Peak recorded wind gusts across west central Utah included 66 mph at the Delta Municipal Airport and 58 mph at the U.S. 6 at Eureka sensor.

The peak recorded wind gust across southwest Utah was 61 mph at the Milford ASOS. In addition, these strong winds caused low visibilities in blowing dust. On Interstate 15 between Parowan and Beaver, this led to accidents involving 13 vehicles, resulting in multiple injuries.

A wildfire began just north of Cedar City and was fueled by strong winds, before being contained after burning 45 acres. A landowner had been doing a controlled burn on April 24, and thought had put it out, but some of the embers reignited the blaze with the strong winds and got out of control on April 25. The fire threatened, but did not reach, 30 homes in the area. The wildfire consumed three power poles and caused a power outage; Rocky Mountain Power estimated the damage at $15,000.

Peak recorded wind gusts from the Cache Valley included 64 mph at both Lewiston and at the Logan ASOS. Large tree limbs and branches were knocked down across most of the valley, with some downed branches causing power outages in several cities, as well as blocking some roadways. Lewiston Elementary School sustained some minor cosmetic damage from the wind. A warehouse in Logan had its roof blown completely off, and several other roofs sustained damage. Several barns were also blown over, including one in Richmond near Pepperidge Farm.

Peak wind gusts across the northern Wasatch Front included 72 mph at the I-15 at Tremonton sensor, 66 mph along I-15 at the Willard Point of Entry, 63 mph at Antelope Island, 61 mph at both Brigham City and Plymouth, and 60 mph at Bothwell. The strongest winds near Tremonton toppled two large semitrailer trucks, seriously injuring one of the two drivers. Many large trees were also knocked over across the area, and the wind sent several trampolines flying out of backyards.

Peak recorded wind gusts across the Salt Lake and Tooele Valleys included 86 mph at Vernon Hill, 82 mph at South Mountain, 72 mph in Draper, 67 mph at the Great Salt Lake Marina and University of Utah, and several other locations with gusts in the 55-65 mph range. At a construction site in Murray, an eight-story scaffolding collapsed, damaging some of the building material it was holding. At the same site, large marble panels, weighing 80 to 100 pounds each, were picked up by wind and shattered into sharp shards. The winds also damaged several boats at the Great Salt Lake Marina. Many large trees were uprooted, with trees and branches causing power outages when they fell on power lines. A few power poles were knocked over by the winds, and a few power poles also caught fire as a result of the wind and dust brought by the storm. Roof damage was reported in several locations, and roofs were completely blown off of outbuildings in Vernon and Grantsville. Trampolines, fences, and garage doors were also commonly damaged objects in this storm. The wind was blamed for several traffic accidents across the area, both due to low visibilities in blowing dust, as well as due to tree branches falling onto roadways.

The strongest wind gusts in Utah Valley occurred after the cold frontal passage, with peak recorded gusts of 73 mph in Lehi, 66 mph in Saratoga Springs, 65 mph in Highland, and several other gusts in the 50-65 mph range. Several large trees were knocked over by the wind, especially in the Lehi area. In addition, the flagpole in front of the Eagle Mountain city office was blown over.

events.cz_name: GREAT SALT LAKE DESERT AND MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Peak recorded wind gusts across Utah's northwest desert included 82 mph at Wendover Peak, 76 mph at Camel Back Mountain and Upper Cedar Mountain, 74 mph at Diddle Knoll, 72 mph along Interstate 80 at Milepost 1, and many other wind gusts in the 60-70 mph range.
Two sensors in the Heber City area recorded particularly strong wind gusts, with a 63 mph gust at Heber City Municipal Airport - Russ McDonald Field, and 58 mph at the US-40 at Heber sensor.
The Interstate 15 at the Sevier River sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 66 mph.
Peak recorded wind gusts across west central Utah included 78 mph at the U.S. 6 at Eureka sensor, 73 mph at Fish Springs, and 61 mph at Fillmore Municipal Airport.
Peak recorded wind gusts in southwest Utah included 64 mph at the Milford ASOS, 62 mph at Brimstone Reservoir, and 60 mph at the Cedar City ASOS.
Hail with a diameter of 0.75 inches was reported near Clarkston, Utah.
The Delta Bus Garage sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 62 mph.
The White Reef RAWS recorded a maximum wind gust of 65 mph.
A windy thunderstorm moved over Lake Powell, causing a houseboat to be blown into a cliff. One sensor nearby at Bullfrog Marina recorded a peak wind gust of 39 mph.
Peak recorded wind gusts from this thunderstorm included 74 mph at the Leroy sensor and 63 mph at the Coal Road sensor, both in the Wyoming Department of Transportation mesonet.
A visitor to Capitol Reef National Park reported a flash flood in the Cottonwood Wash.
The Fremont Junction sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
A maximum wind gust of 58 mph was reported at the Price ASOS.
A peak wind gust of 59 mph was recorded at the South Valley Regional Airport, previously known as the Salt Lake City Municipal 2 Airport.
A wind gust of 60 mph was recorded at the Utah Department of Transportation State Route-248 sensor.
The Hole-In-Rock SNOTEL recorded 1.50 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 18 inches of new snow.
The Clear Creek #1 SNOTEL received 1.40 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 17 inches of new snow.
On the northern edge of the storm system, northeasterly downslope winds developed across the northern Wasatch Front. Multiple wind gusts of 58 mph were recorded at a sensor in Farmington.
Strong northerly winds were observed on the northern end of Utah County, with a sensor in Saratoga Springs recording a peak wind gust of 65 mph.

events.cz_name: GREAT SALT LAKE DESERT AND MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Several strong wind gusts were recorded in Utah's northwest desert in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet, including 62 mph at Diddle Knoll, 59 mph at the sensor West of Wildcat Mountain, and 58 mph at both Camel Back Mountain and Upper Cedar Mountain.

The combination of strong winds and heavy snowfall caused hazardous travel conditions in west central Utah. In Delta, the Bus Garage sensor recorded a maximum wind gust of 62 mph. In Fillmore, 5.2 inches of snow was recorded for the entire storm. On Interstate 15 near Cove Fort, multiple automobile accidents were reported in the early afternoon of May 11, including a rollover accident, a four-car accident, and multiple trucks that got stuck in the snow on the interstate.

Strong easterly winds developed in the canyons along the Wasatch Mountains on the morning of May 11, especially in Little Cottonwood Canyon. Wind gusts of 72 mph were recorded at the peak of Mount Baldy, and 58 mph wind gusts were recorded at the base of Alta Ski Lifts. Near Alta Ski Lifts and Snowbird Ski and Summer Resort, multiple large trees were knocked down by these winds.

Heavy snowfall in southwest Utah triggered many automobile accidents, knocked out power to thousands, and caused widespread tree damage. Cedar City received 12 inches of new snow, and reports of 5-10 inches of snow were common across the area. Dozens of large tree limbs were knocked down, primarily in the Cedar City area, and the tree damage was multiplied by the fact that leaves had already grown in most locations by early May. Travel was greatly impacted by the snowfall, especially along the Interstate 15 corridor between Beaver and Cedar City, where the Utah Highway Patrol reported 21 crashes, 19 slide-offs, and a semitruck rollover in an eight hour period on May 11. Power outages were widespread, and as many as 7,000 people had their power knocked out, primarily due to snow-laden limbs falling into power lines.

events.cz_name: UTAHS DIXIE AND ZION NATIONAL PARK
events.event_narrative: Strong northeasterly winds developed in Utah's Dixie, with the White Reef RAWS recording a peak wind gust of 73 mph. In addition, several trampolines were blown from yards, and some fence and roof damage was reported. A few power lines were knocked down by the winds, and nearly 4,000 people lost power in several cities across the area.
The Pine Creek SNOTEL received 2.70 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 27 inches of new snow.

The Yankee Reservoir SNOTEL received 2.40 inches liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 24 inches of new snow. Travel was impaired due to snowfall along several routes in the southern mountains, including State Routes 14 and 20. In addition, State Route 143 east of Brian Head and State Route 148 over Cedar Breaks were closed for the day due to accumulating snow.
The I-80 at Silver Creek Junction sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 65 mph.
Hail ranging from dime sized to nickel sized was observed in both Bluebell and Myton.
Strong thunderstorm winds caused a semitruck to blow over on Interstate 80 at Milepost 16.
A large, healthy tree was snapped half way up the trunk after a strong thunderstorm wind gust.
A large tree was knocked down by thunderstorm winds.
A large tree was broken by a strong wind gust from a passing thunderstorm.
The Interstate 80 at Silver Creek Junction sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 73 mph.
The Interstate 15 at Plymouth sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 63 mph.

A severe thunderstorm moved through the Dugway Proving Ground. Peak recorded wind gusts from this storm included 77 mph at White Sage, 70 mph at Durand Road, 65 mph at Vernon, 64 mph at Fish Springs, and 59 mph at Simpson Springs.
Another severe thunderstorm moved through the Dugway Proving Ground, with peak recorded wind gusts of 61 mph at Juliet Road and 58 mph at Callao Gate.
The Durand Road sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a maximum wind gust of 73 mph.
A maximum wind gust of 60 mph was recorded at the Interstate 80 at Milepost 29 sensor.
A sensor in Tooele recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph.
A peak wind gust of 61 mph was recorded at the Evanston, Wyoming ASOS.
A cold air funnel cloud was spotted over Willard Bay. The funnel did not move over land.

An unseasonably cold storm system brought snowfall to the mountains of northern Utah, with the heaviest snowfall on Tuesday, June 17. The day before this storm, Monday, June 16, four members of an Ogden family left for a backpacking trip in Wheatgrass Canyon in the back country of Weber County. The family was unprepared for the sudden weather shift, and the father of the family, a 46-year-old male, suffered from cold exposure, as well as potential diabetes complications. Two of the family members hiked out of the canyon on Wednesday to find help, but the man passed away before medical teams could return.
The Price ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 66 mph.
The US-40 at Starvation sensor recorded a maximum wind gust of 62 mph.
The Wendover AWOS recorded a peak wind gust of 68 mph.
The Interstate 80 sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 60 mph.
A wind gust of 67 mph was recorded by the Wyoming DOT sensor at Painter.
The Callao sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground's mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 63 mph.
The Causeway sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground's mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph.
A maximum wind gust of 60 mph was recorded at the North Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
The Playa Station sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a wind gust of 60 mph.
A 62 mph wind gust was recorded at the West Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
The North Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet registered a maximum wind gust of 63 mph.

Flash flooding occurred in Zion National Park, with the river gauge at the North Fork of the Virgin River rising to 253 cfs. Park rangers reported that Behunin Canyon, Heaps Canyon, and Pine Creek all experienced flash flooding.
Flash flooding occurred primarily in Pine Creek in Zion National Park. Flows rose to 500 cfs, and the national park recorded the flood on video.

Heavy rain over the Seeley burn scar caused a debris flow, with debris and water crossing State Route 31 near Huntington. This debris shut down the highway, and the excessive runoff and debris also damaged a small debris dam located upstream.
The Promontory Point sensor recorded a maximum wind gust of 72 mph.
The Wig Mountain sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph.
A 60 mph wind gust was recorded at the Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
A sensor in Saratoga Springs recorded a peak wind gust of 62 mph.
The Camel Back Mountain sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a wind gust of 59 mph.
A 63 mph wind gust was recorded at the I-80 at Grassey, UT sensor.
The Five Mile RAWS recorded a maximum wind gust of 76 mph.
The Great Salt Lake Marina sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph.
A flash flood was reported in Nine Mile Canyon and recorded on video.
Flash flooding occurred across Nine Mile Canyon Road, with boulders and mud pushed onto the roadway by the flood waters.
A flash flood occurred on Utah State Route 12 at Milepost 6. The westbound lane was blocked by debris that was about 4 feet deep and 20 feet long.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Zion National Park. Several waterfalls were reported across the park, and flash floods were observed in Birch Creek and multiple other drainages across the southern end of the park.
Flash flooding was observed along Pleasant Creek in Capitol Reef National Park, with the worst flooding at the south end of the Scenic Drive.
Pine Creek, a tributary of the Escalante River, experienced a flash flood due to heavy rainfall. Flows on Pine Creek reached 1000 cfs before the creek flowed into the larger Escalante River.
A flash flood was reported in lower Johnson Canyon after estimated rainfall of more than 2 inches.
Flash flooding occurred in Red Canyon after heavy rainfall, and was recorded on video.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding in multiple neighborhoods in Enterprise, Utah. Street flooding was widespread, and several homes and business were impacted by flood waters. Two homes experienced extensive damage, with basement flooding destroying furniture and other possessions, while other homes had less significant damage.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Eagle Mountain, Utah, specifically in the Cedar Pass Ranch neighborhood. Flood waters were primarily limited to two properties, with one home experiencing significant damage.
Park rangers at Capitol Reef National Park reported flash flooding along Pleasant Creek, the South Draw Road, and the Sheets Gulch area.
Flash flooding occurred along Sulphur Creek and in the main campground at Capitol Reef National Park.
Flash flooding was reported in Croton Canyon near Lake Powell.

Heavy rain fell on an actively burning fire near Levan and caused a debris flow. Mud and debris flowed onto State Route 28 between Levan and Gunnison, shutting down a 12 mile stretch of the road. Flood waters also washed out a campground, and flooded one basement.
Heavy rain on a burn scar near Levan caused a debris flow for the second time in three days. Debris slid onto a portion of State Route 28, temporarily closing the road.
A spotter in West Valley City reported hail with a diameter of one inch.
A tree with a diameter of approximately 3 inches was knocked down by thunderstorm winds in Sandy.
The Painter WYDOT sensor recorded a wind gust of 59 mph.
Half dollar sized hail was reported in Ibapah and Goshen.
The Rosebud RAWS recorded a maximum wind gust of 61 mph.
The Ray's Valley RAWS recorded a peak wind gust of 66 mph.
The sensor at Granite Peak recorded a maximum wind gust of 62 mph.
Peak recorded wind gusts in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet included 62 mph at the Durand Road sensor and 59 mph at Simpson Springs.
The Five Mile RAWS recorded a maximum wind gust of 64 mph.
Nickel sized hail was reported by a member of the public near Grantsville.
Hail with a diameter of one inch fell near the Tooele airport.
Penny sized hail was reported in Riverton.
A maximum wind gust of 67 mph was recorded by the Simpson Springs sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
Penny sized hail was reported in Lehi.
Nickel sized hail was reported near Sunnyside.
Penny sized hail was reported near the LDS temple in Bountiful.
Hail with an average diameter of one inch fell along United States Highway Route 6, north of Helper. The hail accumulated to a depth of 4 inches, requiring the road to be plowed.
Hail with a diameter of 1 to 1.5 inches was reported along Utah State Route 31 in Huntington Canyon, and the hail accumulated to a depth of 6 inches on the roadway.

A large debris flow occurred in Huntington Canyon and flowed onto State Route 31 after heavy rain fell on the Seeley burn scar. Many boulders and trees flowed onto the roadway, with some trees as large as 40 feet in length and 4 feet in diameter. |The area with the heaviest impact was the North Hughes drainage, with significant flooding and debris also occurring in Cabin Canyon and the Old Folks Flat area. It took the Utah Department of Transportation about 24 hours to reopen the roadway to traffic.

Flash flooding occurred in Brookside and Veyo, both of which are towns along the Santa Clara River, during the overnight hours. In Brookside, flood waters washed out roads and caused damage to several garages and basements. Near Veyo, a family of 13 was camping in what had been a dry streambed, when flood waters rose and forced them to higher ground. Tents and other camping equipment were washed downstream, and the waters even picked up their minivan, slamming it into a boulder. All 13 people were rescued, with no injuries reported.
Utah State Route 132 was temporarily closed at Milepost 37 due to flooding and debris on the roadway.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Capitol Reef National Park, including along Pleasant Creek, Sheets Gulch, and Cottonwood Wash. In addition, the Notom Road was impacted by the flooding.
Park rangers reported flash flooding along Sheets Gulch in Capitol Reef National Park.
Flash flooding was reported in the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument, including along the Burr Trail, with mud, rocks, and water flowing across the roadway.

Flash flooding occurred along the Fort Pearce Wash, with recorded flows rising from zero to 7,692 cfs in a very short period of time. This was the 3rd highest recorded flow since 1985. Due to mitigation efforts following previous floods, no damage was reported from these flows.

Heavy rain during the early morning hours of August 20 led to flooding in West Jordan and Murray, with approximately 25 houses reporting some degree of flood damage. This flooding was most common in driveways, garages, and basements, with some homes receiving significant damage.
The Forest Service reported flash flooding in Red Canyon and Butch Cassidy Wash.
Members of the public reported flash flooding in Red Canyon.
Flash flooding was reported in several drainages in Zion National Park, with the worst flooding in Birch Hollow, Heaps Canyon, and Pine Creek.
Isolated street and house flooding was reported in Panguitch, with flooding also reported in nearby dry washes.

Heavy rain over the Seeley burn scar caused flooding in Hughes Canyon and near Electric Lake in Upper Huntington Canyon. Flooding was reported in the lower portion of Huntington Canyon as well, with mud and rocks covering the road near the Huntington  Plant.
Flash flooding closed Utah State Route 29 between Castle Dale and Joe's Valley, with water and rocks covering the roadway.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Capitol Reef National Park, with both Grand Wash and Capitol Gorge experiencing flooding. Rangers also closed the Scenic Drive due to flooding.
Flash flooding occurred on both La Verkin Creek and Dry Creek, with the gauge along La Verkin Creek increasing to 800 cfs.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Zion National Park, with flooding stranding a few hikers in the Narrows until the waters receded. The gauge on the North Fork of the Virgin River rose to 1577 cfs.
Flash flooding was reported in both Johnson Canyon and Buckskin Wash, with road damage in multiple locations across the area.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Washington City, including road flooding along Main Street. At least 6 homes were damaged by flood waters, and flooding also occurred in a grocery store.
Flash flooding occurred along Wahweap Creek, with the Smoky Mountain Road becoming impassable for several hours.

Widespread flash flooding occurred across Carbon County, with damaging floods reported in Helper, Price, Carbonville, Kenilworth, Spring Glen, and Westwood. Damage to public infrastructure totaled $500,000, including damage to bridges, culverts, and roads. Over 100 homes received at least some flood damage, with most of the flooding occurring in basements, yards, driveways, and garages. Damages to these homes totaled in excess of $2 million.

Peak recorded wind gusts from this thunderstorm included 62 mph at the Salt Lake City International Airport ASOS and 59 mph at the Center Tailings sensor. The winds uprooted trees at the International Center and damaged some buildings and private airplanes at the Salt Lake City International Airport.
The Gunnison Island sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 62 mph.
The Legacy Parkway sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph, and damage was reported in South Weber, with several trees uprooted and a small barn heavily damaged by the wind.

The strong thunderstorm that had moved through Salt Lake and Davis counties, continued into Weber County, with maximum recorded wind gusts of 69 mph at Ogden Peak and 59 mph at the Great Salt Lake Minerals sensor.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Cannonville, and the hail ripped through a polycarbonate greenhouse.
In addition to golf ball size hail, the severe thunderstorm moving through Cannonville also had winds strong enough to bend a steel flagpole that was buried in cement.
Flash flooding was reported in Echo Canyon in Zion National Park.
The severe thunderstorm that caused damage due to hail and wind in Cannonville also flooded several roads through the town.
The West Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 67 mph.
The Gunnison Island sensor recorded a maximum wind gust of 65 mph.
The Badger Spring RAWS recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
The Wendover Point of Entry sensor and the Wendover AWOS both recorded maximum wind gusts of 68 mph.
The North Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 72 mph.
A strong thunderstorm moved through Salt Lake City, and the UDOT sensor near the Gateway Mall recorded a peak wind gust of 62 mph.
A 61 mph wind gust was recorded by the sensor at Interstate 80 at Milepost 1.
A 62 mph wind gust was recorded at the Bountiful Bench.
Peak recorded wind gusts in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet included 72 mph at Callao, 61 mph at West Salt Flats, and 59 mph at Interstate 80.
Park rangers in Capitol Reef National Park reported flash flooding along Pleasant Creek.

Widespread flash flooding occurred in Capitol Reef National Park, including a 3 foot rise of water in Sulphur Creek, water 1.5 feet deep in Grand Wash, and water flowing over State Route 24, with several waterfalls along the highway.
Flash flooding was reported along Harris Wash, with a few hikers becoming briefly stranded due to the flooding. A few roads near Hole-in-the-Rock Road were also washed out by the flood waters.

Flash flooding occurred in several drainages in Zion National Park, including Behunin Canyon, Heaps Canyon, and several other canyons in the park. In addition, waterfalls were reported over most of the western end of the park.
Heavy rain over the Clay Springs burn scar caused a minor debris flow, sending rocks and debris onto State Route 125.
Minor flash flooding was reported in Gould's Wash near Quail Creek Reservoir.

Significant flash flooding was reported in several drainages across Kane County, including Warm Creek and Wahweap Creek. The Paria River rose to 1,519 cfs at the southern end of the river, with widespread flash flooding around the headwaters of the Paria due to widespread, long-duration rainfall.

Flash flooding was widespread across Washington county, including flooding reported in the cities of St. George, Washington, and Ivins. The most common flooding occurred in washes and city streets, with several areas experiencing over a foot of water flowing through the streets. Approximately 15 homes were flooded in the St. George area, and a few homes were damaged in Ivins. Flooding also damaged parts of the Southgate Golf Course in St. George. Many parts of Zion National Park experienced flooding, and the park actually shut down for part of the day when mud, debris, and a large boulder slid onto State Route 9, blocking traffic. The North Fork of the Virgin River rose to 4,790 cfs, the 7th highest recorded flow in the river in the last 100 years.

Widespread flash flooding once again occurred in Carbon County, with significant flooding reported in Carbonville, Helper, Kenilworth, Price, and Wellington. The hardest hit area was the Piling's Trailer Court, where at least 24 homes were damaged or destroyed. In total across the county, 53 homes were damaged, including 22 that were declared completely destroyed. In addition, a sewage treatment plant was shut down when it was inundated with 4 feet of water and leaked into the Price River; the damage estimate for the treatment plant was $75,000. Street flooding was widespread across the area, and the Price River overflowed its banks at multiple locations.

Flooding was again widespread across Washington County, with floods reported in Enterprise, Ivins, Santa Clara, St. George, and Springdale, among others. Most rivers and washes in the area experienced flooding, with particularly high flows in the Beaver Dam Wash and the Virgin River. Rock and mud slides were common across the area, temporarily closing several highways across the county. Flooding also occurred across much of Zion National Park, with the park closing for a period of time due to flooding and debris on roadways. This flooding included in the popular Narrows section of the park, where two hikers were stranded by the flood waters; one of the hikers escaped to safety, but the other, a 34-year-old male, died in the flood. ||In Enterprise, many roadways flooded, and a few businesses were damaged by flood waters. In Ivins, a few homes near 600 S and 400 W experienced flooding. In St. George, damage was most severe at the Southgate Golf Course, with the majority of holes inundated with water.
Heavy rain over the Seeley burn scar caused a debris flow onto Utah State Route 30, closing the highway for an extended period of time until the debris could be cleared.

Persistent moderate to heavy rainfall caused flash flooding along the Paria River, especially near Kodachrome Basin State Park. The flood waters undercut the road into the state park, and caused a bridge over the river to collapse. When this occurred, a couple visiting from Italy was crossing the bridge, and their car fell into the river. The car was carried about 150 yards downstream before flipping onto its top. The couple, a 47-year-old female and a 62-year-old male, managed to escape out of a back window before being rescued. Both were taken to the hospital to be treated for hypothermia. The loss of the bridge caused most of Kodachrome Basin State Park to remain closed for an extended period of time.

events.cz_name: GREAT SALT LAKE DESERT AND MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Winds were strong for several hours across Utah's west desert, and the strongest winds were post-frontal northwesterly winds. Peak recorded gusts included 65 mph at Wendover Peak, 62 mph at Diddle Knoll in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet, and 61 mph at Promontory Point.

Peak recorded wind gusts across the Salt Lake and Tooele valleys included 76 mph at the Interstate 80 at Milepost 78 sensor, 74 mph at Vernon Hill, and 65 mph at the Great Salt Lake Marina. In addition, these high winds caused problems for high profile vehicles traveling along Interstate 80. Two semitrucks were knocked over by the strong winds, both near Milepost 78. One of the trucks was pulling two trailers, and this accident closed Interstate 80 for a couple of hours. In addition, a pickup truck pulling a trailer also flipped onto its side along the same stretch of Interstate 80. High winds also caused power outages, with nearly 2,000 homes and businesses losing power during the event. Some tree damage was also reported over western portions of the Salt Lake Valley.

events.cz_name: GREAT SALT LAKE DESERT AND MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Peak recorded wind gusts from the Great Salt Lake and Utah's northwest desert included 81 mph at Badger Island, 77 mph at Hat Island and Upper Cedar Mountain, 74 mph at Wendover Peak, 73 mph at Camel Back Mountain, and 65 mph at Simpson Springs and English Village in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
Peak recorded wind gusts in west central Utah included 61 mph at Fish Springs and 58 mph in Fillmore.
Maximum recorded wind gusts in southwest Utah included 61 mph at the Milford ASOS and 58 mph at the Cedar City ASOS.
The sensor at Fort Bridger, Wyoming recorded a maximum wind gust of 58 mph.
Peak wind gusts in the Cache Valley included 63 mph at Wellsville and 62 mph at Logan.

events.cz_name: GREAT SALT LAKE DESERT AND MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Maximum wind gusts near the Great Salt Lake Desert included 63 mph at Promontory Point and 61 mph at Wendover Peak.

events.cz_name: GREAT SALT LAKE DESERT AND MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Strong wind gusts were recorded in Utah's northwest desert both pre-frontally and post-frontally, with peak recorded gusts of 69 mph at Wendover Peak, 62 mph at Wendover Airport and Camel Back Mountain, 60 mph at Rosebud and Upper Cedar Mountain, and 59 mph at Promontory Point.

The Tony Grove Lake SNOTEL received 2.90 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 30 inches of new snow. In addition, winds were strong on the mountain peaks across northern Utah, with a maximum recorded wind gust of 91 mph at Ogden Peak.

The Cottonwood Canyons received steady snowfall through much of this event, with Snowbird Ski and Summer Resort, Brighton Resort, and Alta Ski Lifts all measuring a storm total of 30 inches new snow. In addition, Mount Baldy recorded a peak wind gust of 80 mph.
The Trial Lake SNOTEL received 2.20 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 24 inches of new snow. In addition, the Chepeta RAWS recorded a peak wind gust of 76 mph.

events.cz_name: GREAT SALT LAKE DESERT AND MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Peak recorded wind gusts included 63 mph at Upper Cedar Mountain and 58 mph at Diddle Knoll.
The Cedar City ASOS recorded a maximum wind gust of 62 mph.

events.cz_name: GREAT SALT LAKE DESERT AND MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Strong postfrontal winds developed in Utah's northwest desert, with peak recorded wind gusts of 75 mph at Diddle Knoll, 70 mph at Upper Cedar Mountain, and 62 mph at Promontory Point.
Liberty received 13 inches of new snow from the storm.

Storm totals from the northern Wasatch Mountains included 18 inches at Snowbasin Resort and 15 inches at Powder Mountain. In addition, the Tony Grove Lake SNOTEL received approximately 22 inches of new snow. Winds were also strong on the mountain peaks, with the Snowbasin Straw Top sensor recording a peak gust of 89 mph.

Storm total snowfall totals included 28 inches at Alta Ski Lifts, 23 inches at Snowbird Ski and Summer Resort, and 18 inches at Brighton Resort. Winds were also strong on the mountain peaks, with Mount Baldy recording a peak wind gust of 96 mph.
The Trial Lake SNOTEL received 2.20 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 17 inches of new snow. In addition, the Chepeta RAWS recorded a maximum wind gust of 95 mph.
The Mammoth-Cottonwood SNOTEL received approximately 20 inches of new snow for the storm.
The Buck Flat SNOTEL received approximately 21 inches of new snow for the storm.
Storm total snowfall in the Cache Valley included 7 inches in Richmond and 6 inches in North Logan.

Storm total snowfall along the northern Wasatch Front included 12 inches at Bountiful Bench, 10 inches at Centerville, 9 inches at Northeast Ogden Bench and Bountiful, and 5 to 7 inches at many other locations.

The highest snow totals in the Salt Lake Valley were on the benches, especially early in the event. On the valley floor, many locations received just a trace of snow with the initial cold front early Christmas morning, but steadier snow developed through the day to create higher totals. Storm total snow amounts included 14 inches in Sandy, 13 inches in Cottonwood Heights, 12 inches in Upper Millcreek, 8 inches in Olympus Cove and the Upper Avenues, and 5 to 7 inches in many locations, including most of Salt Lake City proper.
Storm total snow amounts in the southern Wasatch Front included 13 inches at Suncrest, 11 inches at the Spanish Fork Powerhouse, 7 inches in Nephi, and 6 inches in both Alpine and Provo.
The heaviest snowfall in the Wasatch mountain valleys occurred in the Ogden Valley, with 12 inches of new snow reported in Liberty. Heber City also received 7 inches of new snow.
Powder Mountain received 17 inches of new snow from the storm. In addition, the Parrish Creek SNOTEL received 2.10 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 25 inches of new snow.
Storm total snow reports in the Cottonwood Canyons included 27 inches at Snowbird Ski and Summer Resort, 21 inches at Alta Ski Lifts, and 14 inches at Brighton Resort.
The Huntington Horse SNOTEL received approximately 19 inches of new snow for the event.
Parts of west central Utah received significant snowfall with this storm, including 12 inches of snow in Fillmore and 11 inches in Oak City.
Cedar City received the most snowfall in southwest Utah, with parts of the city reporting 7 inches of new snow.
The Pine Creek SNOTEL received 2.10 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 36 inches of new snow.
The Yankee Reservoir SNOTEL received 1.60 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 27 inches of new snow.
Storm total snowfall along the northern Wasatch Front included 9 inches at Bountiful Bench, 8 inches in Centerville and Fruit Heights, 7 inches in Farmington, and 6 inches in Clearfield.

Strong downslope winds developed along the northern Wasatch Front, with peak recorded wind gusts of 78 mph in Farmington, 76 mph at the sensor at US-89 near Lagoon, 69 mph in Centerville, and 59 mph at Bountiful Bench. The winds knocked over a total of three semitrailers on Legacy Parkway and Interstate 15, and some damage to road signs, fences, and trees was also reported, including at least one large tree that blew onto a parked car. Winds also caused power outages across the area, with at least 4,000 customers losing power, mostly in Farmington, Centerville, and Ogden.

The storm brought heavy snowfall to the Salt Lake Valley on December 28 and 29, and then the storm was prolonged in the Tooele Valley into December 30 due to the development of additional lake effect snow. Storm total snowfall included 7 inches in Tooele and 6 inches in both Salt Lake City and Cottonwood Heights.

Gusty downslope and canyon winds developed in the Salt Lake Valley on the morning of December 30. While these winds were not as strong as further north along the Wasatch Front, wind gusts did reach as strong as 60 mph at the University of Utah. Isolated damage to fences and trees was reported, including one tree as large as 4 feet in diameter that was blown over. In addition, winds caused power outages across the area, with over 4,000 customers in Salt Lake City temporarily losing power.
The Parrish Creek SNOTEL received 1.10 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 20 inches of new snow.
Storm total snowfall in the Cottonwood Canyons included 23 inches at both Snowbird Ski and Summer Resort and Alta Ski Lifts, as well as 18 inches of new snow at Brighton Resort.

Bullfrog Basin received 8.7 inches of snow from this event, which is especially noteworthy because this location has averaged 4 inches of snow for all of meteorological winter over the past 45 years. Note that this event began in December 2014.

Bullfrog Basin received 8.7 inches of snow from this event, which is especially noteworthy because this location has averaged 4 inches of snow for all of meteorological winter over the past 45 years. Note that this event continued into January 2015.
Escalante received 9 inches of new snow from the storm. Note that this event continued into January 2015.
Escalante received 9 inches of new snow from the storm. Note that this event began in December 2014.
The Lookout Peak SNOTEL received 1.50 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 18 inches of new snow.

Storm total snow reports included 26 inches at Alta Ski Lifts, 25 inches at both Brighton Resort and Snowbird Ski and Summer Resort, 19 inches at the Park City Mountain Resort summit, 18 inches at Big Cottonwood Spruces, and 17 inches at both Provo Canyon and Solitude Mountain Resort.
Strong easterly canyon winds developed along the northern Wasatch Front, with peak wind gusts of 68 mph at US-89 near Lagoon and 62 mph at Farmington.
Gusty canyon winds also developed in the Salt Lake Valley, with a peak recorded wind gust of 62 mph at the Mouth of Parley's Canyon.
Heavy snow fell across portions of southwest Utah, where Cedar City received 17 inches of new snow and New Harmony reported 12 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: UTAHS DIXIE AND ZION NATIONAL PARK
events.event_narrative: Accumulating snowfall was reported in an area that rarely gets snow, with 2 to 3 inches of snow reported in Washington City, Ivins, and St. George.
Heavy snow fell across much of south central Utah, including 16 inches of snow at Kodachrome Basin State Park and 9 inches of snow at both Kanab and Tropic.
Brian Head Resort reported 15 inches of new snow, and the Kimberly Mine SNOTEL reported 1.70 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 25 inches of new snow.
The Kolob SNOTEL received 2.10 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 21 inches of new snow. In addition, Brian Head Resort reported 14 inches of snow for the storm.
Storm total snowfall of 13 inches was reported in Cedar City.
Kodachrome Basin State Park recorded 11 inches of new snow for the storm.

Following a very dry and warm winter, two friends wanted to take advantage of the fresh snowfall from early March, so they decided to go snowboarding at Snowbasin Resort on March 4. On one of their runs, they made their way out-of-bounds of the resort in an area called Hells Canyon. On their way out of this terrain, one of the snowboarders, a 21-year-old male, triggered an avalanche. He was caught and buried in the avalanche, while his trailing friend stayed out of the path and was able to find help. However, when the body of the victim was found an hour later, he was determined to have injuries incompatible with life, and he passed away that day.
Thunderstorms that formed near the cold front helped produce a 58 mph wind gust at the Promontory Point sensor.
The Great Salt Lake Marina sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph ahead of the cold front.

Snow totals from the storm included 12 inches on Bountiful Bench, as well as 9 inches in both North Ogden and Centerville. Automobile accidents in the northern Wasatch Front were not as widespread as in the Salt Lake Valley, but 10 weather-related accidents were reported in Davis County.

Storm total snow amounts included 8 inches in Millcreek, 7 inches in The Avenues, and 6 inches of snow in South Salt Lake. In addition, automobile accidents were widespread across the area, with Utah Highway Patrol counting 88 accidents in Salt Lake County between midnight and 5 p.m. on March 3, including 13 accidents with injuries.
Storm total snow amounts in the Ogden Valley included 14 inches at Liberty and 11 inches of new snow at Eden.

Storm total snowfall included 19 inches at Powder Mountain and 17 inches at Snowbasin Resort. In addition, the Farmington SNOTEL received 2.50 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 25 inches of new snow.

Snow totals included 24 inches at Brighton Resort, 20 inches at Alta Ski Lifts, 18 inches at Provo Canyon, and 16 inches at both Solitude Mountain Resort and Canyons. In addition, there was a significant traffic accident on a snowy Interstate 80 near Lamb's Canyon, when an SUV crashed at high speed into the back of a Utah Department of Transportation maintenance truck. A Utah Department of Transportation employee in the truck sustained minor injuries, but the SUV driver experienced significant injuries, requiring him to be flown to a local hospital.
The Trial Lake SNOTEL received 1.50 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 18 inches of new snow.
The Timberline SNOTEL received 1.90 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 22 inches of new snow.
Cedar City received a storm total of 18 inches of snow, with the heaviest snowfall occurring the night of March 1 into the morning of March 2.
Kodachrome Basin State Park received a storm total of 23 inches of snow, with the heaviest snowfall occurring on the morning of March 2.
The Mount Baldy SNOTEL received 2.10 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 25 inches of new snow.
The Kolob SNOTEL received 3.20 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 35 inches of new snow.

A human-caused grass fire erupted in Murray, along the Jordan River in the Hunter Woods area. The fire threatened several homes, but firefighters were able to stop the blaze before it reached the residences. A few homes did receive smoke damage from the fire, and approximately 1,200 feet of vinyl fencing was destroyed. The fire also destroyed a walking bridge in the area.
Flash flooding occurred in Zion National Park, particularly along Pine Creek. In addition, many waterfalls were reported across the park.
The Interstate 15 at Beer Creek sensor recorded a maximum wind gust of 58 mph.
The Logan-Cache Airport ASOS recorded a maximum wind gust of 60 mph. Minor tree damage was also reported from the strong winds.

Peak recorded wind gusts in the northern Wasatch Front included 64 mph at the  	Brigham City Airport, 64 mph at Hill Air Force Base, 63 mph at the I-15 at Plymouth sensor, and 61 mph along the Legacy Parkway. The winds tore the roof off of a couple buildings in Bountiful, and more minor damage was reported to trees, fences, and trampolines that became airborne. Several power outages occurred across the area, impacting at least 4,000 people.

Maximum wind gusts recorded in the Salt Lake and Tooele valleys included 81 mph at the Great Salt Lake Marina, 75 mph at Baccus Highway, 66 mph at Point of the Mountain, 66 mph at the Interstate 15 at 2400 South sensor, 65 mph at Salt Air, and 64 mph at the Salt Lake City International Airport ASOS. A semitrailer was overturned on Interstate 215 in Salt Lake City, and several large trees were uprooted across the Salt Lake Valley. Winds also caused damage to many fences and yards across the area, including displacing sheds and knocking over at least one cinder block wall.  Salt Lake City International Airport had an internal ground stop of 1 hour and 45 minutes total due to the strong winds; 25 aircraft were held for up to 63 minutes, with an average of a 30 minute delay, and at least 16 flights were diverted to other airports. Power outages were common across the area, with at least 9,000 customers impacted in Salt Lake County and over 2,000 customers impacted in Tooele County.
Peak recorded wind gusts included 61 mph at Saratoga Springs and 58 mph at Pioneer Crossing. Minor tree and fence damage was reported across Utah Valley from the winds.

The peak recorded wind gust in the Wasatch mountain valleys was 60 mph in Morgan, Utah. Minor damage occurred to trees in the area, and nearly 2,000 people experienced power outages caused by the winds.
The Interstate 15 at Sevier River Northbound sensor recorded a maximum wind gust of 65 mph.

Peak recorded wind guts included 71 mph at the U.S. 6 at Eureka sensor, 62 mph at the Delta Municipal Airport, 61 mph at Fish Springs in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet, and 58 mph at the Clearspot sensor. Blowing dust reduced visibilities and created hazardous driving conditions across the area.

Maximum recorded wind gusts included 63 mph at the Milford Municipal Airport/Ben and Judy Briscoe Field, 61 mph at the Cedar City Regional Airport, and 61 mph at the Brimstone Reservoir RAWS. In addition, a few trees were knocked down across the area due to the strong winds. Power outages were common across Iron County, with over 3,000 customers impacted.

events.cz_name: GREAT SALT LAKE DESERT AND MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: The winds were strongest across Utah's northwest desert, with maximum wind gusts of 82 mph at both Lakeside Mountain and English Village, 81 mph at the Interstate 80 at Milepost 1 sensor, 75 mph at Badger Island, 74 mph at Upper Cedar Mountain, 72 mph at the Wendover Point of Entry, and many observations in the 55-70 mph range. The largest impact was along Interstate 80 near Delle, where low visibility in blowing dust was a major factor in a large pilup crash. A semitruck slowed down when experiencing reduced visibilities, but this caused several passenger vehicles to collide with the back of the truck. After the chain reaction was finished, a total of 6 semitrucks and 11 passenger vehicles were involved in the accident, resulting in 25 injuries, including 18 hospitalizations. There was also one fatality in the crash, a 65-year-old male. The interstate was closed for 6 hours from Milepost 1 to Milepost 99 due to this accident. In separate incidents, several other semitrailers were also knocked over along Interstate 80 due to the strong crosswinds.

The Quakie Haven Fire began near Fish Lake on the afternoon of April 14, and grew quickly due to strong winds. The fire destroyed two summer cabins and damaged several outbuildings and other structures in the Sleepy Hollow area, but fire crews were able to keep the blaze away from other cabins in the area. The fire also forced the temporary closure of portions of State Route 25. Suppression efforts continued for more than a week after the blaze was ignited, but the fire was effectively under control and was no longer threatening structures beginning on the evening of the 14th of April.

A fallen power line ignited a brush fire in the Avenues area of Salt Lake City, which quickly grew to 100 acres due to strong winds. Ten homes were evacuated near 700 North and I Street. Firefighters were able to quickly contain the blaze, keeping it from reaching any of the homes, but one home suffered heat damage in the outside patio area, and a second house suffered smoke damage.
Logan received a storm total of 11 inches of snow, with many other locations across Cache Valley measuring 5-10 inches of snow.
Storm total snowfall included 12 inches in Bountiful, 12 inches on the Northeast Ogden Bench, 11 inches in Ogden, and many other reports along the northern Wasatch Front of 5-10 inches of snow.

Storm total snowfall in the Salt Lake Valley included 14 inches at Upper Millcreek, 12 inches in Sandy, and many reports of approximately 10 inches of snow. The worst conditions on roadways occurred on the morning commute of April 15, with 118 crashes reported, including 16 that resulted in injuries. During the evening commute on April 15, a woman was killed in a multicar crash on State Route 201 near the Interstate 80 on-ramp. The victim lost control of her vehicle on the snow-packed road, and was then rear-ended by another vehicle traveling the same route. In addition, a Utah Highway Patrol trooper was injured while responding to the scene.

The Parrish Creek SNOTEL received 2.00 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 25 inches of new snow. In addition, winds were strong during the beginning of the storm, with peak wind gusts of 88 mph at Ogden Peak, 85 mph at the SR-65 at Big Mountain Pass sensor, and 84 mph at Powder Mountain.

Storm total snowfall amounts included 45 inches at Snowbird Ski and Summer Resort, 34 inches at Alta Ski lifts, 23 inches at Big Cottonwood Spruces, and 22 inches of snow at Brighton Resort. In addition, winds were strong at the beginning of the storm, with peak recorded gusts of 89 mph at Arrowhead Peak at Sundance Mountain Resort, and 75 mph at Jupiter Peak near Park City.

Several SNOTEL stations in the Uinta Mountains received 0.80 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 13 inches new snow, including Hewinta SNOTEL and Steel Creek Park SNOTEL. In addition, winds were strong at the beginning of the storm, with maximum wind gusts of 87 mph at Windy Peak and 81 mph at Lofty Lake Peak.

The Mount Baldy and Red Pine Ridge SNOTELs both received 1.70 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation, or approximately 20 inches of new snow. In addition, a peak wind gust of 75 mph was recorded at Dog Valley.
The Aragonite RAWS recorded a maximum wind gust of 61 mph.
Penny sized hail was reported near Big Water.
The Bryce Canyon RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 67 mph.
The SR-12 at Boulder Summit sensor recorded a maximum wind gust of 60 mph.
The Milford ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph.
A 61 mph wind gust was recorded at the West Granite sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
Nickel sized hail was reported in Sandy.
The Clifton Flat RAWS recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph.
Half dollar sized hail was observed and photographed in the Pariette Wetlands south of Myton, Utah.
Nickel sized hail was reported near Sandy, Utah.
Ping-pong ball sized hail was observed and photographed in Honeyville.
A 58 mph wind gust was recorded at the Center Tailings sensor.
Lightning struck a house in Syracuse, Utah in the morning hours of May 28. The roof of the house caught fire, but was seen and extinguished quickly, leading to only relatively minor roof damage.

Heavy rain caused widespread flash flooding in the cities of Gunnison and Centerfield, with an approximate total of 30 homes and businesses sustaining some damage from the flood waters. About another 100 homes experienced yard flooding. Most damaged homes had minor damage to basements or lower levels. In addition, portions of the Gunnison Market grocery store were flooded, and some of the inventory was damaged.
Flash flooding was reported along Wahweap Creek and some surrounding drainages.
Flash flooding was reported along the East Fork of the Virgin River, particularly closer to Orderville and US 89.
Flash flooding occurred along the Paria River, with a peak flow of 2050 cfs recorded at the Paria River gauge near Kanab.

A strong thunderstorm produced an outflow that continued southward well beyond the original storm. Observed wind gusts along this outflow included 66 mph at the West Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet and 60 mph at the Salduro UPR sensor.
The Interstate 80 sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a maximum wind gust of 66 mph.

A strong thunderstorm moved through northern Box Elder County, with a maximum recorded wind gust of 62 mph at the I-84 at White's Valley sensor. This thunderstorm caused significant damage in the town of Portage, Utah, with several trees damaged or knocked down and approximately ten homes with shingle damage. In addition, a porch awning collapsed, injuring a woman and sending her to the hospital.
A maximum wind gust of 62 mph was recorded at the SR-30 mesonet site.
The Rosebud RAWS recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph.
The SR-85 at Dannon Way sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
The North Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a maximum wind gust of 60 mph.
A peak wind gust of 62 mph was recorded at the Center Tailings sensor.
A 66 mph wind gust was recorded by the Legacy Parkway sensor.
One inch diameter hail was reported near Clarkston.
Hail up to the size of ping pong balls was reported near Promontory, north of the Great Salt Lake.
Nickel-sized hail was reported in Cornish, Utah, near the Idaho border in Cache Valley.
Nickel-sized hail was reported in Providence.
Strong thunderstorm winds knocked down several large trees throughout the Cache Valley, including near the cities of Logan and Cornish.

Strong thunderstorms pushed through far northern Utah, producing a peak wind gust of 64 mph at the Curlew Junction sensor. In addition, this storm damaged an irrigation system near Snowville and downed many tree branches in the area.

A strong thunderstorm produced severe winds across the northern end of the Great Salt Lake, with peak recorded gusts of 65 mph at the I-15 at Plymouth sensor, 62 mph at Promontory Point, and 58 mph at the I-15 at Tremonton sensor. In addition, trees were knocked down as the storm moved through Garland, including one tree that fell onto a car.

Multiple sensors on the west end of the Salt Lake Valley recorded severe wind gusts with a passing thunderstorm, including 71 mph at the Mountain View at Dannon Way sensor, 64 at the Baccus Highway sensor, and 58 mph at the Trans-Jordan Landfill sensor. In addition, one of these microbursts made it to the Salt Lake City International Airport, with a recorded wind gust as high as 70 mph on the FAA Midfield sensor. These winds caused significant impacts to the terminal, with a total of 837 minutes of holding time on the ground, 11 flight diversions, several planes that had to circle the airport, and 3 flight cancellations.
One inch diameter hail was reported at the Capitol Reef National Park visitor center.
Hail the size of nickels was reported along Utah State Route 14 near Duck Creek Village.
Heavy rain fell on the Patch Springs Fire burn scar, causing a debris flow along the southern end of the scar, with debris flowing all the way to Johnson Pass Road.
A large flash flood was reported in Sheets Gulch in Capitol Reef National Park.

A large flash flood occurred along Wahweap Creek, particularly near the town of Big Water. The flood waters closed and damaged roads near Big Water, and stranded people at the Big Water Visitor Center for 3 hours.
Flash flooding was reported along the Buckskin and House Rock Valley drainages, as well as a few other smaller drainages in the area.
Flash flooding overnight was reported across a wide area of drainages flowing into Lake Powell.
Flash flooding occurred along the Paria River, with the river gauge recording a peak flow of 2520 cfs.
Flash flooding was reported along the Scenic Drive of Capitol Reef National Park. Rangers closed the road when water from Grand Wash began flowing over the roadway.

Significant flash flooding was reported in several locations along Lake Powell, including at Wahweap Creek, at Iceberg Canyon, and at Crystal Springs Canyon. Many visitors were stranded for several hours while they waited for the flood waters to subside. The most dramatic flooding occurred in Crystal Springs Canyon, where visitors to the lake watched as three of their boats were tossed around and damaged by the flood waters. One of these boats, a 23-foot 1997 Maxum, was hit and submerged by two boulders, and was considered a total loss after the event.

Park rangers at Goblin Valley State Park reported flash flooding along the Temple Wash, with Temple Mountain Road severely washed out at the Temple Wash crossing. Flood waters from Temple Wash and Chute Canyon also crossed Little Wild Horse Road.
The Flattop Mountain RAWS recorded a peak wind gust of 70 mph.
A maximum wind gust of 69 mph was recorded at the Otter Creek RAWS.
The Bullfrog Marina sensor reported a wind gust of 60 mph.
A peak wind gust of 68 mph was recorded at the Center Tailings sensor.
The West Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet reported a wind gust of 60 mph.
The Rattlesnake Bench sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
Flash flooding was reported during the overnight and morning hours along Wahweap Creek.
Another large flash flood was reported along the Paria River, this one extending into the upper drainages of the river, as well as a few other nearby drainages.
Flash flooding occurred along the Paria River, with the river gauge rising to 1160 cfs.
Heavy rain fell on the Patch Springs burn scar, leading to a large debris flow that traveled 4 miles to reach State Route 196.
A 58 mph wind gust was recorded at the Great Salt Lake Marina.
The Hat Island sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 65 mph.
Peak wind gusts across the Great Salt Lake Desert included 71 mph at the Interstate 80 at Milepost 78 sensor and 61 mph at the Upper Cedar Mountain sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
The Badger Island sensor recorded a maximum wind gust of 69 mph.
Park rangers at Zion National Park reported significant rises on the North Fork of the Virgin River, particularly through the Narrows. Hikers were temporarily stranded until the waters receded.
Zion National Park rangers reported flash flooding along Clear Creek.
Large flows were reported along the East Fork of the Virgin River, with the gauge near Springdale measuring flow rates as high as 1140 cfs.

A large line of thunderstorms moved through the Wasatch Front overnight on July 8, into the early morning hours of July 9, with the northern Wasatch Front getting hit the hardest by heavy rainfall. Flash flooding along roadways was reported in several locations, including along Interstate 15 and on Parrish Lane in Centerville, where water was up to four feet deep. One house in Woods Cross received significant flood damage, with all the possessions in the basement declared a total loss.
Peak recorded wind gusts from this thunderstorm included 72 mph at Vernon Hill and 66 mph at the APG sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
Maximum recorded wind gusts from this thunderstorm included 77 mph at the Wendover AWOS and 58 mph at the Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
Flash flooding was reported along Johnson Wash.
Heavy rain over the Patch Springs Fire burn scar caused a debris flow in the area.

Multiple rounds of heavy rain caused significant flash flooding in Capitol Reef National Park. The Scenic Drive was closed due to water and debris impacting the road in multiple locations, particularly at the Grand Wash and near the Slick Rock Divide. Major flooding occurred in Capitol Gorge, and caused significant damage to the dirt road to Capitol Gorge, such that the road to this popular hiking area was closed for more than two months after the flood. Very heavy flows were also reported along Sulphur Creek and Pleasant Creek, as well as all associated washes, with water a foot deep in Sulphur Creek.
Heavy rain over the Seeley Fire burn scar caused flash flooding and debris flows onto State Route 31.
Nickel-size hail was reported near Meeks Cabin Reservoir, along the Utah/Wyoming border.
Penny to nickel size hail was reported near Parowan.

Strong thunderstorm winds impacted Interstate 80 with a 72 mph gust recorded at the Interstate 80 sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet and a 64 mph wind gust recorded at the Interstate 80 at Milepost 29 sensor.
The Flattop Mountain RAWS recorded a maximum wind gust of 69 mph.
A peak wind gust of 72 mph was recorded by the Joe's Valley RAWS.

A 21-year-old male was riding a paddle board on the reservoir at Rockport State Park when a strong wind gust caused by a thunderstorm moved through the area. The victim was separated from his group of friends and drowned in the reservoir. His body was recovered the next day. The strongest wind gusts recorded from nearby sensors included 52 mph at the Interstate 80 at Silver Creek Junction sensor and 45 mph at the Interstate 80 at Wanship sensor.

Park rangers reported flash flooding in Zion National Park, particularly in the Pine Creek drainage. The Virgin River had significant rises from Zion National Park down to St. George, with the river gauge at St. George rising from near 30 cfs up to 2310 cfs. Flooding was also reported in several other locations across the county, including Washington City, Bloomington, and St. George, with at least a dozen different roads in these areas receiving some level of flooding throughout the event.
Heavy rain caused significant flooding in Hildale, with flood waters damaging both a few roads and a few homes across the area.
The Diddle Knoll sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
A line of thunderstorms moved through northern Utah, and a maximum wind gust of 59 mph was recorded at the Lakeside Mountain sensor.
A 59 mph wind gust was recorded at the Upper Cedar Mountain sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.

A thunderstorm dropped very heavy rainfall near Woodland Hills and, combined with saturated soil from large amounts of rain the previous day, produced a large mudslide across the area. The mud damaged the basement of one home and also invaded five other properties, with extensive mud clean-up necessary on private driveways and along Skylake Drive. A total of 14 homes were evacuated as a precaution immediately following the mudslide.

Park rangers at Capitol Reef National Park reported flash flooding at multiple locations in the park. Flooding first occurred along Sulphur Creek, and then a second thunderstorm initiated flash flooding along Grand Wash, with flood waters reaching Highway 24.
Park rangers reported flash flooding in the Pine Creek slot canyon, with extreme used to described the flooding.

Very heavy rain caused a massive flash flood along Wahweap Creek. The flood wave was caught on video and it carried full size dead trees left over from previous smaller floods, along with boulders the size of cars.
A large flash flood was reported in the Wahweap drainage, north of Big Water.

Heavy rain over northern Davis County caused widespread street and parking lot flooding, particularly in Farmington and Layton. In addition, several homes in Fruit Heights experienced basement flooding.
Quarter to ping pong ball sized hail was observed and video taped along Interstate 84 north of Bothwell.
Strong thunderstorm winds destroyed a wooden barn in Bothwell.
The White Reef RAWS recorded a peak wind gust of 60 mph.
Several large trees were knocked down by thunderstorm winds near Henefer.

Peak recorded wind gusts as the line of thunderstorms moved through Salt Lake County included 65 mph at the Great Salt Lake Marina, 64 mph at Parley's Canyon, and 63 mph at the Salt Lake City International Airport. In addition, the strong winds hit the finish line of the Tour of Utah bike race, where many had gathered for a medal ceremony. A large metal structure was knocked over by the winds, and two people were injured.
Peak recorded wind gusts in Davis County included 65 mph in Farmington and 61 mph at the Centerville UDOT sensor.
Maximum recorded wind gusts in Weber County included 62 mph at the Great Salt Lake Minerals sensor and 61 mph at Ogden Peak.
The SR-65 at Big Mountain Pass sensor recorded a peak wind gust of 80 mph.
Peak wind gusts from the line of thunderstorms in Box Elder County included 76 mph at Lakeside Mountain, 66 mph at the Utah Test and Training Range Oasis Compound, and 60 mph at Hat Island.
The Wendover AWOS recorded a peak gust of 79 mph.
The North Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a maximum wind gust of 68 mph.
The West Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph.
The West of Wildcat Mountain sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a wind gust of 69 mph.
The Lower Cedar Mountain sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a maximum wind gust of 59 mph.
A 64 mph wind gust was recorded at the Camel Back Mountain sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
The Portable RWIS 5 sensor, located northeast of Lakeside along Interstate 80, recorded a maximum wind gust of 64 mph.
A 76 mph wind gust was recorded at the Lake Point at Interstate 80 sensor.

Significant flash flooding was reported in Capitol Reef National Park, with multiple flood waves reported along Sulphur Creek. Flash flooding also occurred in both Spring Canyon and Chimney Rock Canyon. The Spring Canyon flooding was generally between 6 inches and two feet deep, though it reached as high as 5 feet deep through the narrow section. Water flowing through Chimney Rock Canyon was reported to be one foot deep.
A few medium sized trees were knocked down by strong thunderstorm winds near Logan, with one tree falling onto a car.
The Brimstone Reservoir RAWS recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph.

A family was having a picnic in a park in Lehi, Utah, when a thunderstorm moved across the area. Lightning struck a nearby tree, and critically injured a 50-year-old woman. No one else in the party was seriously injured, but the victim passed away in a hospital a few days later.

A thunderstorm producing heavy rain moved over Hildale, Utah in the early afternoon, producing flash flooding along Short Creek and other neighboring drainages. This water flooded Highway 59, and portions of the road were closed and gated off, as this is a somewhat common occurrence for the community. However, a second strong thunderstorm trained through the area, producing very significant flooding out of Maxwell and Jans Canyons.||This second flood swept across a group of 16 people who had been waiting for the initial flood waters to recede. When the second flood began, the group retreated to the two vans they had been traveling in, and the large flood swept the vans away and down the channel. Three of these people were rescued and survived, but the remaining 13 people were killed by the flood. Three of these 13 victims were women, while the remaining 10 were children under the age of 12.||Property damage was also extensive across the area, including damage to water lines, area roadways, power lines, bridges, and other infrastructure. In addition, multiple private homes had flood and mud damage, while several others had minor water damage. Multiple vehicles were also destroyed in the flood.
Heavy rain caused a debris flow from the Patch Springs burn scar, with debris covering State Route 199 at Johnson Pass.
Flash flooding occurred along the Paria River, with the gauge at Lees Ferry rising from near 100 cfs up to 2064 cfs.
Park rangers at Zion National Park reported flash flooding through the area, with the worst flooding near the Emerald Pools. Waterfalls and minor rockfalls were also reported across the park.
Additional heavy rainfall over Hildale caused minor flash flooding across the area while search and rescue operations were still ongoing from the previous day's major flood.

Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall brought flash flooding to Zion National Park, including along North Creek, but the most notable flood occurred in Keyhole Canyon. A group of seven people entered Keyhole Canyon in the early afternoon, planning to travel through the small but popular canyoneering route. Flooding in Keyhole Canyon occurred quickly; no one in the group was able to escape the canyon or get to higher ground, and the flood killed all seven individuals. The seven victims were between 51 and 59 years old.
The Callao sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph.
The Causeway sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet recorded a maximum wind gust of 66 mph.
A peak wind gust of 64 mph was recorded at the West Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
A 72 mph wind gust was recorded at the North Salt Flats sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.
The Wendover Airport AWOS recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
The Gunnison Island mesonet site recorded a maximum wind gust of 68 mph.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding across Hildale, with multiple roads damaged by the flood waters. Debris was flowing along the shoulder of State Route 59 between Milepost 0.5 and Milepost 1.0, and minor flooding occurred along Carling Avenue and Utah Avenue. In addition, several homes reported basement flooding.

Flash flooding was reported in several locations across Zion National Park. This flooding included the Emerald Pools area, but most of the flooding occurred on the east side of the park, including Spry Canyon, Pine Creek Canyon, and a few other small canyons nearby.
Flash flooding was reported along Wahweap Creek, Buckskin Gulch, and the lower portions of the Paria River.

Flash flooding was reported in several locations, including Deer Creek and Calf Creek. The Dirty Devil gauge at Poison Springs rose from 23 cfs to 1176 cfs, and part of Hole-in-the-Rock Road was washed out.
Flash flooding was reported in Capitol Reef National Park, with one foot of water over the Capitol Gorge Road.

Heavy rain brought road, parking lot, and basement flooding to the Sugarhouse and Foothill areas of Salt Lake City. The flooding damaged multiple streets including Roxberry Road, Sherwood Drive, and 1300 South near 2500 East. There was also a significant amount of water on Foothill Drive, particularly near 2200 South. Approximately six homes also experienced basement flooding across the area.
Flash flooding was reported in Lehi, with some flooded residential roadways. In addition, approximately six homes sustained flood damage, primarily to basements.

Lightning struck a home in Cedar City and started a fire in one corner of the house. Firefighters were able to put out the fire relatively quickly, but not before the residence sustained approximately $8,000 worth of damage.

Heavy rain brought road, parking lot, and basement flooding to the Sugarhouse and Foothill areas of Salt Lake City. The flooding damaged multiple streets including Roxberry Road, Sherwood Drive, and 1300 South near 2500 East. There was also a significant amount of water on Foothill Drive, particularly near 2200 South. Approximately six homes also experienced basement flooding across the area.

Peak wind gusts in the Salt Lake and Tooele valleys included 69 mph at South Mountain, 68 mph at Vernon Hill, 66 mph in Tooele, 64 mph at Stockton Bar, 62 mph at the Interstate 80 at Milepost 78 sensor, and 60 mph at both the Mouth of Parleys sensor and the Great Salt Lake Marina sensor. The high winds also knocked out power for over 5,000 customers, with multiple power lines broken by the strong winds. The winds also knocked down several branches in Tooele valley, and launched a trampoline into a neighbor's yard.

events.cz_name: GREAT SALT LAKE DESERT AND MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Peak recorded wind gusts across Utah's northwest desert included 70 mph at the English Village and Upper Cedar Mountain sensors in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet, 64 mph at Promontory Point, and 59 mph at the Utah Test and Training Range sensor. These strong winds knocked over two semitrucks on Interstate 80, and semis were subsequently banned from that stretch of Interstate 80 for the rest of the day.
Maximum recorded wind gusts in west central Utah included 63 mph at the U.S. 6 at Eureka sensor, and 59 mph in the Tule Valley.
The Cedar City ASOS recorded a maximum wind gust of 60 mph, while the Milford ASOS reached a peak of 58 mph.

The strongest winds in the Salt Lake and Tooele Valleys occurred with the cold frontal passage, with peak wind gusts of 62 mph at Vernon Hill, 60 mph at Point of the Mountain, and 58 mph at Flight Park South.

Strong downslope winds occurred in Castle Country after the cold front passed through the area. Maximum recorded wind gusts included 80 mph at the SR-72 at Hogan Pass sensor and 70 mph at Fremont Junction.

events.cz_name: GREAT SALT LAKE DESERT AND MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Strong post-frontal winds were observed near the Utah/Nevada border, with maximum recorded wind gusts of 70 mph at the Interstate 80 at Milepost 1 sensor, 62 mph at Interstate 80 at Milepost 29 sensor, and 62 mph at the Interstate 80 sensor in the Dugway Proving Ground mesonet.

The Salt Lake Valley received almost no snow from this event, but the Tooele Valley was hit hard on the morning of November 16, with generally 8 to 10 inches reported across Tooele City. The snow caused significant travel delays and impacts in the Tooele area with snow quickly accumulating on roadways, most notably along Utah State Route 36. In addition, the heavy snow broke many large tree branches across the area.

Snowfall in Utah County had a strong south to north gradient, with Levan in the southern end of the county receiving 9 inches of snow, while locations from Provo northward generally received an inch or less. Snow primarily fell during the day on November 16, with a little snow lingering into November 17.
Heavy snow fell over the Sanpete Valley, with Fairview and Mount Pleasant both receiving 10 inches of snow.
Fillmore received 8 inches of snow from the storm, while Eureka reported 6 inches of snow.

Strong winds developed in the Uinta Mountains, with peak recorded wind gusts of 83 mph at the Chepeta RAWS and 77 mph at the Dry Ridge sensor.

Strong easterly canyon and downslope winds developed along the northern Wasatch Front, with peak recorded wind gusts of 70 mph at the Portable RWIS #2 sensor, 65 mph in Farmington, and 64 mph in Centerville. Only minor damage was reported in the area, including some tree limbs knocked down, as well as minor fence and siding damage.
