Power lines were snapped in Murray, with multiple large trees uprooted throughout town.  Carport and car damage occurred, as did damage to business signs and rooftops.
A wind gust of 74 mph was recorded in Bountiful.

In Salt Lake City, flooding with water in excess of a depth of 6 inches, occurred at the intersection of 100 S and 300 E. Flooding also occurred in common areas of a complex at 300 S and 300 W.
Video received showed 2 to 3 feet deep water flowing down a street in Hildale, eroding a portion of the road.

Video received showed significant flows through a normally dry wash just south of Tropic, including a mature fully grown tree floating beneath an underpass along Bryce Highway. In addition, Bryce Canyon National Park officials reported the closure of the Queens Garden Trail, Navajo Loop, and the road to Bryce Point due to flooding.
Zion National Park officials reported flash flooding in portions of the park, including the  Narrows, Kolob Canyons, and Telephone Canyon.
Hildale dispatch reported 10 power poles down throughout the city, along with multiple downed trees. Time estimated by radar.

The manager of Veyo Pool Resort reported a 7 foot rise on the Santa Clara River. Campsites were evacuated near the river.
The Iron County Emergency Manager reported flooding in Parowan. Floodwaters moved protective concrete barriers for the power plant and pushed them into the power plant  building.

Video received showed deep and swift moving water flowing westward down Center Street and 700 E in Paragonah. Flows originated from Red Creek, which empties into Paragonah from the east. Radar estimated up to 2.15 inches of rain upstream over the Red Creek drainage.
A tree fell on a power line in Greenville.

The Iron County Emergency Manager reported six feet of water flowed over a flood control barrier in Paragonah, resulting in flash flooding in the city. Several homes were flooded. Fifty people were stranded in Red Creek Canyon east of the city.
Heavy rainfall of 1.05 inches was observed in about 55 minutes.

Thunderstorm outflow winds generated blowing dust with near zero visibility along Interstate 15 near milepost 152 south of Fillmore. This resulted in a multi vehicle pileup with at least 22 vehicles involved, 8 fatalities, and 10 injuries. The nearest mesonet site located 7 miles south of the crash site recorded a wind gust to 32 mph around the time of the crash, at approximately 430 PM MDT.
A significant flash flood wave in Pine Creek was reported by Zion National Park staff.
Water flowed across many roadways in Cedar City, including across Interstate 15 near milepost 59.
A video showed flash flooding at the confluence of Birch and North Creeks into the Escalante River.
The Escalante River gauge near Escalante indicated a rise from 3 CFS to 1060 CFS, a rise of 4 feet.
Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument officials reported that significant damage was sustained on House Rock Road near Wire Pass due to flash flooding.
A received video showed a flood wave with significant debris moving through Big Water, UT.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a rise from 23 CFS to 1450 CFS with the primary flood wave.  The time above 1000 CFS was from 2315 MDT to 0130 MDT.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding across Scenic Drive in multiple locations, including Grand Wash and across State Route 24, closing the road. A muddy debris flow was also reported in Sulphur Creek.
Social media video showed strong winds, small hail, and heavy rain in Penrose.  A garage door was damaged.  The peak wind gust was estimated at 60 mph.
LANDSPOUT. A weak, but well-formed, landspout tornado was observed in multiple videos shared via social media.
The Five Mile automated weather station recorded a peak wind gust of 67 mph. The gust appeared to be associated with a microburst from a decaying thunderstorm.
Hail up to 1.25 inches in diameter fell at the Canyon Breeze Golf Course in Beaver.

Several reports of flash flooding in and around Escalante, including Birch Creek. Storm spotters reported logs and trees floating in the Escalante River just north of Escalante. Time of event coincident with time of first report.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported 5 inches of debris, mud, and gravel overflowing the Scenic Drive by the Capitol Gorge area. High-flowing water was also reported in a usually dry wash at the end of the Scenic Drive. Scenic Drive was closed beyond Grand Wash.
The U.S. Highway 6 State at Route 123 automated weather station recorded a wind gust of 61 mph.
A Zion Nation Park ranger reported significant flash flooding occurred on Taylor Creek at the north end of the Kolob Canyon area of the park during the night.

The Interstate 15 at Beaver Ridge automated weather station recorded 0.78 inches of rain  in 10 minutes.  Flooding and debris was reported along State Route 153 between Main Street and the Canyon Breeze Golf Course.
Rainfall total fell in 75 minutes.
Water flowed over State Route 24 between mileposts 102 and 105.
The Interstate 15 at Milepost 29 automated weather station near Browse recorded 1.70 inches of rain in 70 minutes. A 10 minute total of 0.90 inches was recorded.

Washington County dispatch officials reported water over the road on State Route 17 near Toquerville, briefly closing the road.  The bridge where water crossed the road is above full grown trees in the creek below, indicating a significant rise in water level.
Hildale Fire Department dispatch personnel reported water flowing over three street crossings. The streets were closed due to the flows.

Zion National Park dispatch personnel reported numerous slot canyons experienced flooding, including Pine Creek and Spry Canyon. The Zion automated weather station recorded 1.29 inches of rain in one hour. In addition, the East Fork Virgin stream gauge on the East Fort Virgin River near Springdale recorded a peak flow of 2790 CFS.
Zion National Park officials reported a tree fell on a building.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Sunglow Canyon.
A tree fell on a power line.
Summit Park received 0.60 inches of rain in 10 minutes.

The Iron County Emergency Manager reported up to 2.5 feet of water on streets in Enoch, as well as water breaching into homes. The water was deepest near Homestead Boulevard. Several homes were flooded.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a rise from 27 CFS to 493 CFS in 15 minutes, a rise of 1.5 feet.
Law enforcement officials reported a debris flow moved through the Pinnacles and Promised Land Resort areas.
A debris flow was reported into the Elk Ridge area.
The Virgin stream gauge on the Virgin River at Virgin spiked from 108 CFS to 2180 CFS, a rise of over 3 feet.
Basement flooding occurred in 3 homes in Randolph.

A 9-year-old boy was found dead in a vehicle in American Fork on Wednesday, July 21, at around 1:45 p.m. It is believed the child was inside the car for approximately two hours before he was discovered. Temperatures in the vicinity of American Fork at the time were generally in the 90-95 degree Fahrenheit range.
The Paria River near Kanab gauge recorded a peak flow of 865 CFS.
An observer reported 3 feet of rocks, mud, and water flooded into a ranch basement and nearly moved a second home off its foundation near the Crawford Mountains.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding on Sulphur Creek and the Fremont River, along with muddy conditions on Scenic Drive. The initial flood wave through Sulphur Creek contained black boulders.
County dispatch reported Kingston Canyon was underwater with rock and debris over a portion of state Route 62.

Widespread flash flooding occurred in Enoch and Cedar City, with up to 300 homes damaged by flood waters.  Water rescues were performed, and cars were swept off the road.  Interstate 15 was closed during the event.  Numerous roads were eroded by floodwaters, and Fiddlers Canyon was reported underwater.
In Tooele, 37 homes were flooded. Additionally, multiple roads were closed due to flooding.
Flash flooding was reported on the Bountiful Bench, with water flowing through a home.

A significant flood wave carrying debris moved down Bear Creek Canyon, sweeping away mining vehicles at the Gentry Mountain Mine. Several miners were caught in the flood waters, with one miner able to save himself by clinging to a tree a quarter mile down the drainage. Another miner was not able to escape the flood waters and was found deceased 6 miles downstream. Another Mine car was flipped 8 times in the flood waters, but the miners were able to kick out the windows and escape. Significant infrastructure damage occurred at the Mine.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Grand Wash.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding on several drainages in the Park.

Multiple roadways across the greater Salt Lake Valley were flooded. A portion of Interstate 80 was closed near 1300 East, as was Interstate 215 near Millcreek.
Several lane on Interstate 15 near Bountiful were closed due to standing water. Hill Field Road near Hill Air Force Base was flooded.  Basement flooding occurred in Centerville.
Numerous reports, videos, and photos of water over roadways near Utah Valley University in the vicinity of Interstate 15 were received.
Photos from broadcast media indicated water and mud over a roadway in Kanab.
A viewer submitted a video that showed quarter-sized hail.

The Paria River near Kanab gauge rose 3.3 feet, with an increase in flow from 4 CFS to 1790 CFS.

Flash flooding was reported on Coal Creek. The Coal Creek near Cedar City gauge rose from 8 CFS to 1160 CFS overnight. Several homes within the Flying L Ranches subdivision outside of Cedar City were damaged by floodwaters.
Flash flooding carried debris across Old U.S. Highway 91 through Kanarraville.
The North Fork of the Virgin River near Springdale spiked from 26 CFS to 1560 CFS in just 15 minutes, corresponding to a rise of 4 feet.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Grand Wash, Capitol Gorge, and Pleasant Creek were all closed due to flash flooding.

Parley's Creek in Sugarhouse Park overflowed its banks, with water across the park road. The eastbound lanes of Interstate 215 at 3300 South were closed due to flooding for two hours. Water flowed across Silver Bowl Drive in Herriman, with two basements flooded. Significant urban flooding occurred at Willowbrook Condos, with basements flooded.  Additionally, Little Cottonwood Creek flooded.
State Route 89 was briefly closed due to standing water on the road at milepost 171.
A portion of Soldier Canyon Road was destroyed, and thus closed, due to flooding.

Flash flooding produced significant trail damage in Bryce Canyon National Park. Park officials reported the Wall Street section of Navajo Loop, the Bryce Connector Trail, and Peekaboo Loop were closed were closed due to the damage.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Notam-Bullfrog Road was washed out and impassible due to flash flooding south of Sandy Ranch at Dog Water Wash.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Burr Trail, Strike Valley, and Halls Creek Road were all impassible due to flash flooding.
A dike collapse due to heavy rainfall led to a large amount of debris across Old U.S. Highway 91, with the road being closed.
Zion National Park officials reported the Kolob Canyons section of the Park was closed due to significant mud and rock slides from overnight flash flooding.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding of the East Fork of the Virgin River. The flood wave started near the East Fork of the Virgin River near Glendale, which rose from 16 CFS to 544 CFS, corresponding to a 3 foot rise. The flood wave grew downstream from additional heavy rain, where the East Fork of the Virgin River near Springdale rose from 45 CFS to 2410 CFS, corresponding to a 6 foot rise.
The Escalante River near Escalante gauge indicated an increase in flow of 1440 CFS, corresponding to a rise of over 5 feet.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Scenic Drive was closed at Grand Wash due to a large amount of mud across the road, deposited by flash flooding, making it impassible. Rangers also estimated Pleasant Creek and Sheets Gulch had 6-8 feet of flooding overnight, and Burro, Cottonwood, and 5 mile Washes had 2 to 4 feet of flooding overnight.

Zion National Park dispatch officials reported a rockslide due to excessive rainfall along the Scenic Drive north of the Visitor Center. A portion of the road was damaged due to the slide, and was closed as a result. In addition, the river gauge on the North Fork of the Virgin River near Springdale had a sharp rise and peaked at 1690 CFS, corresponding to a rise of over 3 feet.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Notam-Bullfrog Road was washed out at Bullfrog Creek Crossing near Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, resulting in a 5-foot drop-off, making the road impassible.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Grand Wash, with 6 to 8 inches of rapidly flowing water.
Widespread basement flooding occurred in and around Delta.  An observer reported a 2-day rainfall total of 5.83 inches.

events.event_narrative: In the wake of a thunderstorms complex, winds increased across the Great Salt Lake Desert and Mountains. Automated weather station recorded peak wind gusts included 68 mph at Interstate 80 at Knolls, 63 mph at Callao, and 62 mph at Wildcat Mountain.

A tornado first touched down in North Salt Lake at Redwood Road and 900 W around 628 PM MDT. The tornado moved to the northeast through a mix of industrial and residential areas. The tornado produced EF0 damage (winds 65 to 85 MPH) to numerous trees and several homes in the Cloverdale neighborhood. The tornado continued to move off to the northeast, producing more EF0 damage to the Woods Cross Public Works building and a nearby construction site. The tornado reached peak intensity along 1100 W, producing EF1 damage (winds 86 to 110 MPH) where it uprooted a healthy mature tree and leaned a wooden power pole. The tornado continued to the north, weakening, but still producing EF0 damage before lifting off the ground.||The tornado then made a second touchdown in a field near 800 W where it produced EF0 damage to a business in the area and began moving northward along 800 W. Tree damage and minor property damage indicative of an EF0 tornado was widespread along this swath. Large diameter tree limbs (in excess of 12 inches) were broken off and deposited throughout the area. The tornado then dissipated in the area of 1500 S and Interstate 15 around 634 PM MDT.||The rating for this tornado is EF1 with winds as high as 110 MPH. The tornado had an intermittent track length of about 2 miles over 7 minutes and a max-width of approximately 350 yards with an average width of approximately 150 yards.

The Dirty Devil - Poison Springs Above Hanskville gauge indicated a rise from a baseline around 500 CFS to 14100 CFS, or from a gauge height of about 8 feet to about 21 feet. According to United States Geological Survey, the peak flow rate of 14100 CFS ranks as the 6th highest peak flow rate for all water years back to 1948. The peak gauge height of 21 feet ranks as the 3rd highest peak gauge height for all water years back to 1948.

A significant flash flood occurred in the town of Hanksville, with nearly every structure in town impacted by flooding. Floodwaters were reportedly as deep as 6 feet in places. events.event_narrative: Snow Squall. Visibility at Curlew Junction dropped to 1/4 mi with wind gusts to 37 mph. A webcam showed the road quickly became snow covered.

Snow Squall. Numerous automated weather station along the stretch of Intersate 80 in Uinta County, Wyoming reported snow squall conditions with visibilities of 1/4 mile or less and wind gusts 30 mph or higher. The worst conditions were observed at Evanston-Uinta County Airport - Burns Field, where the visibility fell below 1/4 mile and winds gusted to 61 mph.

Snow Squall. Automated weather stations around Brigham City reported visibilities to 1/4 mile or less and wind gusts around 30 mph. Webcams in the area showed roads became quickly snow covered and impacted the evening commute.

Snow Squall. Automated weather stations along Intersate 15 between the Willard Port of Entry and Hill Air Force Base reported visibilities between 1/8 and 1/4 mile and wind gusts up to 40 mph. Traffic cameras showed roads became quickly snow covered, and traffic data from the Utah Department of Transportation showed significant travel impacts during the evening commute.

Snow Squall. Automated weather stations in the Salt Lake Valley reported widespread visibility reductions to 1/4 mile or less and wind gusts up to 48 mph. In addition, traffic data and webcams showed severe impacts to travel during the evening commute.

Snow Squall. Automated weather stations along the Interstate 80 corridor in Uinta County, Wyoming reported visibilities of 1/4 or less and wind gusts of 30-50 mph in association with a snow squall. Webcams showed snow covered roads.

Snow Squall. Automated weather stations in the Utah Valley reported visibility to 1/4 mile or less and wind gusts 30 to 35 mph with a snow squall, particularly at Point of the Mountain and Pioneer Crossing areas and in Spanish Fork.
